# googleworkspace_group_alias (Resource)

An additional email address (alias) for a Google Workspace group. Mail sent to the alias is delivered to the group as if it were sent to the group's primary address, which suits role addresses such as `trips@` that should reach an existing list.

Aliases cannot be changed in place, so changing either attribute removes the alias and adds a new one. Removing an alias stops mail delivery to that address.

~> **The address must be free.** An alias cannot be an address that a user or group in the organization still uses, as its primary address or as an alias ([Add or delete an alternate email address](https://support.google.com/a/answer/33327), [Resolve duplicate account conflicts](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/p/duplicate-account-errors)). To move an address from a user or group to this group, delete or rename that user or group and remove the old alias first (renaming a user keeps the old address as an alias), in an earlier apply than the one that adds this alias: Terraform does not order deleting one resource before creating an unrelated one.

Google allows up to 30 aliases per group, reserves some local parts (such as `abuse`, `admin`, `postmaster`, and `webmaster`), and notes that alias changes can take up to 24 hours to reach mail delivery ([Give a group an additional alias address](https://support.google.com/a/answer/2727156)).

~> **Requirements:** the service account's domain-wide delegation must include the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group` scope, which the provider requests by default.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "googleworkspace_group" "hiking" {
  email = "hiking@example.org"
  name  = "Hiking"
}

# Mail to trips@ and outings@ reaches the hiking@ list. Neither address may
# still be used by a user or group, as its primary address or as an alias.
resource "googleworkspace_group_alias" "trips" {
  group_id = googleworkspace_group.hiking.id
  alias    = "trips@example.org"
}

resource "googleworkspace_group_alias" "outings" {
  group_id = googleworkspace_group.hiking.id
  alias    = "outings@example.org"
}

# To fold a retired group's address into this list, remove the old group in
# one apply and add the alias in a later one. In a single apply Terraform may
# add the alias before deleting the group, and Workspace rejects the alias
# while the address is still in use.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `alias` (String) The alias email address, in one of the account's domains. It must not be in use by any user or group. Changing this forces a new alias.
- `group_id` (String) Immutable ID of the group, e.g. `googleworkspace_group.example.id`. Changing this forces a new alias.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite ID, `<group_id>/<alias>`. Used for import.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imported as "<group_id>/<alias>". The group's email address also works in
# place of its ID and is resolved to the ID on import.
terraform import googleworkspace_group_alias.trips 01234567890abcde/trips@example.org
terraform import googleworkspace_group_alias.outings hiking@example.org/outings@example.org
```
